source_text: {ΚΥΡ.} Οὐκοῦν ἐρῶ μὲν, ὡς ἔνι· σὺ δὲ δὴ αὖ, εἴ τι παρεκθέοιμι τῆς ὁδοῦ, συγγνώμων ἔσο· δριμὺς γὰρ ὁ λόγος, καὶ ἀμυδρὸν τὸ αἴνιγμα. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Σύμφημι. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἀνατυπούσης ἡμῖν, ὦ Παλλάδιε, τῆς τοῦ σώματος κεφαλῆς, ὡς ἐφ' ἑαυτῇ, τὸν νοῦν· ὧδε γὰρ ἐδόκει τῷ θείῳ τε καὶ ἱερῷ Γράμματι· τὰς ἐξ αὐτοῦ τε καὶ ἐν αὐτῷ φυσικῶς ἀνισχούσας ἐννοίας, δι' ὧν εἰς εἴδησιν τὴν ἐφ' ὅτῳ οὖν τῶν ὄντων χειραγωγούμεθα, θριξί τε καὶ κόμαις παρεικάζομεν. Ταυτὶ γὰρ ἡμῖν τὰ ἐκ κεφαλῆς ἀναβρύοντα. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Μεμνήσομαι. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἀκειρεκόμης οὖν ἄρα καὶ ἐν ἡμῖν οἱονείπως ὁ νοῦς, καὶ Θεῷ κατάκομος, ἐννοιῶν ὑπάρχων ἐπίμεστος ἀγαθῶν. Γυμνὸς δὲ δὴ αὖ καὶ ἐψιλωμένος, καὶ ἀτιμώτατον φαλάκρωμα νοσῶν, εἰ μήτε ὀρθὰς ἐπὶ Θεῷ τὰς διαλήψεις ἔχοι, μήτε μὴν ἐφ' ἅπασι τοῖς πρακτέοις ἀρίστην τε καὶ ἀκατάψεκτον καταπλουτήσει τὴν εἴδησιν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἀληθές· ταυτὶ γὰρ ἡμῖν καὶ ἀρτίως διεγυμνάζετο. {ΚΥΡ.} Οὐκοῦν πρὸ μὲν τῆς τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἐπιδημίας κέκληται πρὸς θεογνωσίαν διὰ Μωσέως ὁ Ἰσραήλ. Ταύτῃτοι καὶ ἡγιάζετο. Ηὔξατο δὲ τρόπον τινὰ τῷ Θεῷ τὴν εἰς ἁγνείαν εὐχήν. Ὅτι γὰρ ἔσται νομοφύλαξ, ἐπηγγέλλετο σαφῶς ἐν τῷ ὄρει Χωρὴβ, οὕτω λέγων· «Καὶ πάντα ὅσα εἶπε Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς, ποιήσομεν καὶ ἀκουσόμεθα.» Ἦν οὖν ἄρα νομικῆς παιδεύσεως τὸν νοῦν ἔχων ἀνάπλεω, καὶ οἱονεὶ κομῶντα Θεῷ, τῆς διὰ Μωσέως ἐντολῆς τὰ αὐχήματα. Ἀλλ' ἐμιάνθησαν ἐπὶ νεκρῷ· Ἀπεκτόνασι γὰρ τὸν Ἐμμανουήλ· καὶ ἅγιος μὲν ἀληθῶς ὁ Χριστοῦ θάνατος, μολυσμὸς δὲ τοῖς ἀπεκτονόσιν ἦν τὰ τῆς κυριοκτονίας ἐγκλήματα. Ξυρᾶσθαι δὴ οὖν ὁ νόμος αὐτοῖς ἐπιτάττει λοιπὸν, οἷά τινα κόμην, τὴν ἐν νόμῳ παίδευσιν, μονονουχὶ δὲ καὶ ἀποκείρεσθαι τὰ ἐν τύποις κατὰ τὴν ἑβδόμην, τουτέστι, τὰ πρὸ τῆς ὀγδόης, καθ' ἢν ἀνεβίω Χριστὸς, ἀνακαινίζων ἡμᾶς εἰς ἀφθαρσίαν, καὶ εἰς νέαν τε καὶ εὐαγγελικὴν ἀναπλάττων ζωήν. Ἀποκειράμενος τοίνυν τὰ πρὸ τῆς ὀγδόης, ἀνακομᾷ πάλιν καὶ ἁγιάζει τὴν κεφαλὴν μετὰ τὴν ὀγδόην. Ἀνακομᾷ δὲ, οὐκέτι τύποις καὶ σκιαῖς, καθὰ καὶ πρώην, ὁ νοῦς, ἀλλ' αὐτοῖς τοῖς ἐν πίστει καὶ ἀληθείᾳ δόγμασιν. Ἢ γὰρ οὐκ οἰήσῃ δεῖν τοὺς ἐν πίστει δεδικαιωμένους ἀποψιλοῦσθαι μὲν ὥσπερ τῆς ἐν νόμῳ λατρείας τὴν εὐδοκίμησιν, ἀναφῦναι δὲ αὖ, καὶ εἰς νοῦν ἔσω καὶ καρδίαν ἑλεῖν, τῆς εὐαγγελικῆς πολιτείας τὴν εἴδησιν, ὡς ἀμείνω παρὰ πολὺ καὶ προφερεστέραν τῆς ὡς ἐν ἀρχαῖς; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Πῶς ἔφης; {ΚΥΡ.} Οὐ γὰρ δὴ σαφῶς καὶ ἀναφανδὸν ἀνακεκράγει λέγων νομομαθὴς ὢν ὁ Παῦλος, περὶ τῶν ἀρχαίων ἐκείνων καὶ νομικῶν αὐχημάτων· «Ἅτινα ἦν μοι κέρδη, ταῦτα ἥγημαι διὰ τὸν Χριστὸν ζημίαν, ἀλλὰ μενοῦνγε καὶ ἡγοῦμαι τὰ πάντα ζημίαν εἶναι, διὰ τὸ ὑπερέχον τῆς γνώσεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν, δι' ὃν τὰ πάντα ἐζημιώθην, καὶ ἡγοῦμαι σκύ
pass_a_gloss: Cyril: Then I will speak, as far as is possible (ὡς ἔνι); but you in turn, if I should run off somewhat from the road (παρεκθέοιμι), be forgiving; for the account is sharp (δριμύς), and the riddle (αἴνιγμα) dim. Palladius: I agree. Cyril: The head of the body representing (ἀνατυπούσης) for us, O Palladius, as in itself, the mind (νοῦς), for so it seemed good to the divine and holy Writing, we liken to hairs and locks (θρίξ, κόμη) the thoughts (ἔννοιαι) rising naturally out of it and in it, through which we are led by the hand (χειραγωγούμεθα) to knowledge of any one whatever of the things that are. For these are the things springing up for us from the head. Palladius: I will remember. Cyril: Unshorn (ἀκειρεκόμης) then, in us too, in a manner, is the mind, and long-haired for God, being full of good thoughts. But bare in turn and stripped, and sick with a most dishonorable baldness (φαλάκρωμα), if it should have neither right conceptions (διαλήψεις) concerning God, nor be enriched with the best and blameless knowledge concerning all the things to be done. Palladius: True; for these things were also exercised by us just now. Cyril: Therefore before the sojourn (ἐπιδημία) of the Savior, Israel has been called to the knowledge of God (θεογνωσία) through Moses. For this reason he also was being sanctified. And he vowed in a certain manner to God the vow (εὐχή) toward purity (ἁγνεία). For that he will be a keeper of the law (νομοφύλαξ), he was promising clearly on the mountain Horeb, saying thus: 'And all things whatever the Lord God said, we will do and we will hear.' He was then having the mind full of legal training (παίδευσις), and as it were growing hair for God, the boasts (αὐχήματα) of the commandment through Moses. But they were defiled over a dead body; for they have killed the Emmanuel; and holy truly is the death of Christ, but a defilement (μολυσμός) to the killers were the charges of the Lord-killing (κυριοκτονία). So the law commands them henceforth to be shaved, like some head of hair, of the training in the law, and all but (μονονουχί) to crop off the things in types on the seventh, that is, the things before the eighth, on which Christ lived again (ἀνεβίω), renewing us into incorruption, and re-forming us into a new and gospel life. Having cropped off then the things before the eighth, he grows his hair again and sanctifies the head after the eighth. And the mind grows hair again no longer with types and shadows, as also formerly, but with the very teachings (δόγματα) in faith and truth. Or will you not think it necessary that those justified in faith be stripped as it were of the good repute (εὐδοκίμησις) of the worship in law, and in turn grow up again, and take into mind within and heart the knowledge of the gospel way of life (πολιτεία), as better by far and more excellent than the one as at the beginnings? Palladius: How did you say? Cyril: For did not Paul, being learned in the law (νομομαθής), clearly and openly cry out, saying, concerning those ancient and legal boasts: 'Whatever things were gains to me, these I have considered loss on account of Christ; but indeed I also consider all things to be loss, on account of the surpassing of the knowledge of Jesus Christ our Lord, through whom I suffered the loss of all things, and I consider [them] dung' [the word breaks at the column and ends in section 23].
pass_a_gloss_with_greek: ΚΥΡ. ἐρῶ ὡς ἔνι (I will say as is possible); σὺ δὲ συγγνώμων ἔσο (be forgiving) εἴ τι παρεκθέοιμι τῆς ὁδοῦ (if I run aside from the road); δριμὺς ὁ λόγος (the account is sharp/subtle), ἀμυδρὸν τὸ αἴνιγμα (the riddle dim). ΠΑΛΛ. σύμφημι (I agree). ΚΥΡ. the head of the body ἀνατυπούσης (representing) the νοῦς (mind), as Scripture (Γράμμα) held; the ἔννοιαι (thoughts) rising naturally (φυσικῶς ἀνισχούσας) from and in it, by which we are χειραγωγούμεθα (led by hand) to εἴδησις (knowledge) of any of τὰ ὄντα, we liken (παρεικάζομεν) to θρίξ/κόμη (hairs/locks); these ἀναβρύοντα (spring up) from the head. ΠΑΛΛ. μεμνήσομαι (I will remember). ΚΥΡ. so the mind is ἀκειρεκόμης (unshorn) and κατάκομος Θεῷ (thick-haired for God) when ἐπίμεστος ἐννοιῶν ἀγαθῶν (full of good thoughts); γυμνὸς, ἐψιλωμένος (bare, stripped), suffering ἀτιμώτατον φαλάκρωμα (most dishonorable baldness), if it has neither ὀρθὰς διαλήψεις (right conceptions) about God nor is enriched with best and ἀκατάψεκτον (blameless) knowledge of τὰ πρακτέα (things to be done). ΠΑΛΛ. ἀληθές; we were διεγυμνάζετο (exercising) this just now. ΚΥΡ. before the Savior’s ἐπιδημία (coming), Israel κέκληται (was called) to θεογνωσία through Moses; therefore ἡγιάζετο (was sanctified); ηὔξατο (vowed) τὴν εἰς ἁγνείαν εὐχήν (vow to purity); promised at Mount Horeb to be νομοφύλαξ (law-keeper): ‘all that the Lord God said ποιήσομεν καὶ ἀκουσόμεθα (we will do and hear)’. So he had the mind ἀνάπλεω (full) of νομικὴ παίδευσις (legal training), as if κομῶντα Θεῷ (growing hair for God) the αὐχήματα (boasts/glories) of the ἐντολή through Moses. But ἐμιάνθησαν ἐπὶ νεκρῷ (were defiled by a dead body): ἀπεκτόνασι τὸν Ἐμμανουήλ (they killed Emmanuel); Christ’s death ἅγιος ἀληθῶς, but μολυσμός (defilement) to the killers were the ἐγκλήματα τῆς κυριοκτονίας (charges of Lord-killing). So the law commands ξυρᾶσθαι (to be shaved) the ἐν νόμῳ παίδευσις like κόμη, and ἀποκείρεσθαι (crop) τὰ ἐν τύποις on the seventh, i.e. before the eighth, on which Christ ἀνεβίω (lived again), ἀνακαινίζων (renewing) us εἰς ἀφθαρσίαν and ἀναπλάττων (re-forming) into new εὐαγγελικὴ ζωή. Having cropped what precedes the eighth, he ἀνακομᾷ (regrows hair) and ἁγιάζει the head after the eighth; the mind regrows no longer with τύποι καὶ σκιαί but with the δόγματα ἐν πίστει καὶ ἀληθείᾳ. Rhetorical question: must not the ἐν πίστει δεδικαιωμένοι be ἀποψιλοῦσθαι (stripped) of the εὐδοκίμησις (good repute) of λατρεία ἐν νόμῳ, ἀναφῦναι (grow again) and ἑλεῖν (take) into νοῦς and καρδία the εἴδησις of the εὐαγγελικὴ πολιτεία, as far better and προφερεστέρα than that ὡς ἐν ἀρχαῖς? ΠΑΛΛ. πῶς ἔφης; ΚΥΡ. did not Paul, νομομαθής (law-learned), ἀνακεκράγει (cry out) σαφῶς καὶ ἀναφανδόν about the ancient νομικὰ αὐχήματα: ‘ἅτινα ἦν μοι κέρδη ... ἥγημαι ζημίαν ... διὰ τὸ ὑπερέχον τῆς γνώσεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν ... ἐζημιώθην, καὶ ἡγοῦμαι σκύ[βαλα]’ (column breaks inside σκύβαλα).
pass_b_english: Cyril: Then I will tell you as best I can. But you, for your part, must forgive me if I stray at all from the road; for the subject is a subtle one, and the riddle obscure.

Cyril: Since the head of the body, Palladius, represents in itself the mind for us (for so the divine and holy Scripture saw fit), we liken to hairs and locks the thoughts that rise naturally from the mind and within it, by which we are guided to the knowledge of anything that exists, whatever it may be. For these are what spring up for us from the head.
Palladius: I will keep that in mind.

Cyril: So in us too the mind is, in a manner of speaking, unshorn, and has a full head of hair for God, when it is filled with good thoughts. But it is bare and stripped, and suffers a most shameful baldness, if it neither holds right conceptions of God nor is enriched with the best and blameless knowledge of all that ought to be done.
Palladius: True; we were going over this just now.

Cyril: So then, before the coming of the Savior, Israel was called through Moses to the knowledge of God, and for this reason he was also sanctified. And in a certain way he made to God the vow of purity. For at Mount Horeb he plainly promised that he would keep the law, saying: ‘All that the Lord God has spoken we will do and hear’ (Exodus 24:7; Deuteronomy 5:27). So his mind was full of the teaching of the law, and the glories of the commandment given through Moses were, as it were, a head of hair grown for God. But they were defiled by a dead body, for they killed Emmanuel. The death of Christ was truly holy, but for those who killed him the guilt of killing the Lord was a defilement. So the law now commands them to shave off the teaching of the law like a head of hair, and, one might almost say, to crop off on the seventh day whatever was in types (Numbers 6:9), that is, whatever came before the eighth day, the day on which Christ came back to life, renewing us to incorruption and refashioning us for a new life, the life of the Gospel. So, having cropped off what came before the eighth day, he grows his hair again and sanctifies his head after the eighth day (Numbers 6:11). And the mind grows its hair again no longer with types and shadows, as before, but with the very teachings that stand in faith and truth. Or do you not think that those justified by faith must be stripped, as it were, of the good repute won by worship under the law, and must grow anew and take into their inmost mind and heart the knowledge of the Gospel way of life, as far better and more excellent than the way given at the beginning?

Cyril: Did not Paul, a man schooled in the law, cry out clearly and openly about those ancient glories of the law, saying: ‘Whatever things were gain to me, these I have counted as loss for the sake of Christ. More than that, I count all things as loss because of the surpassing worth of knowing Jesus Christ our Lord, for whose sake I have suffered the loss of all things, and I count them…’ (Philippians 3:7–8)

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De adoratione Book 16. Translated afresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withdrawn English was not used for wording.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; a column may cut mid-sentence or mid-word.

Section opens with Cyril’s reply to Palladius’ question at the end of §21. Promise at Horeb: Cyril’s wording has the order ποιήσομεν καὶ ἀκουσόμεθα of Exodus 24:7 LXX (‘we will do and hear’, said at Sinai), while ‘Lord God’ and the name Horeb match Deuteronomy 5:27 (Deuteronomy calls Sinai Horeb, 5:2); both cited; compare also Exodus 19:8 and 24:3. ‘On the seventh day’ and ‘sanctifies his head’ refer back to Numbers 6:9–11 quoted in §21, so Numbers 6:9 and 6:11 are cited at those clauses. ‘Emmanuel’ is a title (Isaiah 7:14), not a quotation; no citation. The Nazirite’s unshorn head (Numbers 6:5) is Cyril’s figure, not quoted; uncited. ‘ἡ ὡς ἐν ἀρχαῖς’ rendered ‘the way given at the beginning’ (the Mosaic way of life). The Philippians quotation continues across the column break: σκύ|βαλα splits, so the English breaks at ‘I count them…’ and §23 resumes with ‘rubbish’. Cyril’s Philippians text reads ‘knowledge of Jesus Christ our Lord’ (NT: Christ Jesus); kept as Cyril gives it.
